newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up on SW heat, outage talk.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up on SW heat, outage talk.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Tuesday, extending yesterday's rally on expectations of air conditioning demand in the U.S. Southwest and talk of power unit outages in the West.

Forecasts called for triple-digit temperatures in the interior part of the Southwest through next week with strong air-conditioning demand, while the Northwest was forecast to experience cooler-than-normal spring weather.
Traders said rumors of a generation unit outage at the Navajo coal-fired plant near Page, Ariz., also pushed futures and short-term physical power prices higher.
"The move was mostly weather-related and the outage talk contributed to it," said a Houston futures trader.

Day-ahead electricity prices for firm, peak delivery at California-Oregon Border (COB) rose $1.50 to $15.50-16.50, while those at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona gained $2.50 to $24.00-25.00.

A spokesman for Salt River Project, which operates the three 750 megawatt (MW) units at the Navajo plant, said Tuesday the units were operating at near half capacity due to low regional electricity demand. Each unit was available for full load, but unit 1 was at 425 MW, while units 2 and 3 were each at 325 MW.
Pacific Gas & Electric Co said its Moss Landing natural gas-fired plant in Monterey, Calif., tripped off line today, and was expected to resume operation Wednesday afternoon.
The Moss Landing station on the central California coast has two units with a total capacity of 1,500 MW.
July PV futures settled up 92 cents at $30.21 a megawatt hour (MWh) after filling a price gap at $29.50-$30.30.
August PV ended up 94 cents at $31.92 near its session high of $32.00. Other PV months finished flat to up 30 cents.
July COB settled up 36 cents at $19.69, trimming a 57 cent gain and partially filling a price gap at $19.50-20.25.
August COB ended up 38 cents at $22.78. Deferred COB contracts finished flat to 25 cents higher.
The complex's upward momentum has also been underpinned by concern over reduced Northwest power supplies to southern California this summer, market sources said.
A Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is expected to introduce a proposal later this week to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system in early July.
The plan called for a summertime rating for the intertie at 6,900 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
In other generation news, the 750 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired plant in Nevada was expected to be on line today following a Saturday shutdown for maintenance.
Startup of a 185 MW unit 1 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was delayed to early Wednesday due to a boiler tube leak.
Also, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was expected to resume output later this week.
NYMEX estimated 904 COB and 902 PV contracts were sold,
((--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
